counterfactual_missing_items: Normal cranial MRI with fine optic nerve cuts
decisive_items: Positive nasopharyngeal swab RT-PCR for SARS-CoV-2
response.rationale: R5 uniquely integrates confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection with the right optic neuritis phenotype (RAPD, central scotoma, impaired color/contrast) and FA optic disc neuritis, making it the most likely diagnosis. R1 is the runner-up because it captures the optic nerve syndrome but omits the etiologic link; R2 is too broad; R3 and R7 describe component inflammation; R6 is unsupported by negative viral serologies.

rejected.why: Positive PCR alone establishes infection, not the ocular diagnosis; no raw support spans.
Uveitis is only a partial finding; it does not explain RAPD, central scotoma, or optic atrophy.
Retinal vasculitis is a component of the presentation, not the unifying diagnosis; it does not explain optic neuritis.
Viral retinitis is not supported; VZV/HSV/EBV/CMV serologies are negative/weakly IgG and no retinitis pattern is described.
